SMTO-POL-0019 — A quick data calculation was too big or took too long

GUID: 206104d3-de73-48c2-b588-bd62688cb395
Slug: operation-limit-guard
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent's small data-processing step was given more than 4 MB of data, or ran past its short time limit, so it was stopped. These quick calculations only work on the data they're given; they don't change your files.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reply asking the Agent to process the data in smaller batches, for example one file or a few thousand rows at a time. Each quick calculation accepts at most 4 MB of input.
  2. If the calculation itself is heavy, ask the Agent to use a regular Python step instead of a quick calculation. Quick calculations have a fixed limit of at most 30 seconds, so heavier work needs a different kind of step.
  3. If small amounts of data also fail, select Copy error details in this panel. The details show whether the data was too large or the calculation ran too long.

What success looks like

  • Each smaller calculation finishes and returns its result.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details, with a rough idea of how much data was involved, to the person who manages SMTO. Changing Model or command timeouts in Settings won't help; this limit is separate.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A python_transform exceeded budget.operation_limits: its serialized inputs were over 4 MiB (rejected before launch) or the worker passed its elapsed-time limit (0.1 to 30 seconds) and was terminated.

What this means

  • Transform input can exceed the 4 MiB admission bound, or a launched transform can exceed its execution-time limit; the receipt distinguishes those phases. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Transform input can exceed the 4 MiB admission bound, or a launched transform can exceed its execution-time limit; the receipt distinguishes those phases.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare input size and executed/failure-stage facts with the transform's time bound; changing a model timeout does not alter this limit.

How to fix it

  • Check the receipt to tell an input-size rejection (before launch) from a timeout (execution/python.py execute_transform). Reduce inputs below 4 MiB, split the computation, or move heavy work to python_action; keep budget.operation_limits enabled, since model and shell timeouts don't affect this limit.
  • Reduce the operation’s input or computational scope. Keep resource limits in place and separate this bound from model and shell timeouts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The reduced transform fits both its input bound and execution-time allowance.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the guard as a routine remedy.
  • Do not substitute a different timeout, permission or model setting for this control.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
